title: Positive-degree exactness of a locally restricted Cech complex
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], I a type, U:I→Opens(X) a family, F an O_X-module sheaf, and D a nonnegative cochain complex of O_X-module sheaves. Let A=Γ(X,O_X), P(W)(V)=F(W∩V), with its restricted A-action, and C=Č(U,P) the full unnormalized categorical Cech complex. Assume natural A-module-presheaf isomorphisms e_p:forget(D^p)≅C^p, with forget(d_D^p) followed by e_(p+1) equal to e_p followed by d_C^p. For each i∈I and p≥0, the restriction of D to U_i is exact in degree p+1. No augmentation is given or required, and no covering hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 1, together with the displayed Cech term and augmentation

proof.text: On an open V⊆U_i, define h on the Cech coordinates by insertion of i at the beginning of the tuple and identify the extra intersection with U_i with V. This gives natural A-linear degree-lowering maps. In positive degrees, compute d h+h d: deletion of the inserted first index gives identity, while deletion of any other index cancels the shifted deletion in the other composite, with opposite signs. Thus positive-degree cocycles are boundaries. The proved TopCat.Presheaf.exactAt_cechComplex_of_le is an alternative source-library implementation of this calculation after identifying the categorical product complex with its concrete Cech complex.

Forget to underlying abelian sheaves before transporting the natural maps through e; e need not be locally O_X-linear. The equations hd give the transported contraction identity. On every V⊆U_i a positive cocycle is therefore a boundary, proving exactness of the underlying abelian sheaf complex. All terms vanish on the empty open, and the argument involves no stalks and no product-stalk interchange.

Use the exact faithful forgetful functor of lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful. Its faithfulness and preservation of kernels and cokernels imply reflection of exactness: the homology object of a short complex forgets to its underlying abelian homology object, and faithfulness reflects a zero identity morphism. Hence the restricted module-sheaf complex is exact at p+1.

theorem cech_sheaf_restrict_exact_positive
    {X : Scheme.{u}} {ι : Type u} (U : ι → X.Opens) (F : X.Modules)
    (D : CochainComplex X.Modules ℕ)
    (e : ∀ p : ℕ, (PresheafOfModules.forgetToPresheafModuleCat (op ⊤) isTerminalTop.op).obj
          (D.X p).val ≅
        ((cechComplexFunctor U).obj
          ((prod.functor (C := X.Opens)).op ⋙ Functor.opHom _ _ ⋙
            (Functor.whiskeringRight _ _ _).obj F.presheafModuleCat)).X p)
    (hd : ∀ p : ℕ,
        (PresheafOfModules.forgetToPresheafModuleCat (op ⊤) isTerminalTop.op).map
            (D.d p (p + 1)).val ≫ (e (p + 1)).hom =
          (e p).hom ≫ ((cechComplexFunctor U).obj
            ((prod.functor (C := X.Opens)).op ⋙ Functor.opHom _ _ ⋙
              (Functor.whiskeringRight _ _ _).obj F.presheafModuleCat)).d p (p + 1))
    (i : ι) (p : ℕ) :
    (((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor (U i).ι).mapHomologicalComplex
      (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj D).ExactAt (p + 1)
